newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget talks to go ahead next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget talks to go ahead next week.

text.p: White House and congressional budget negotiators said on Thursday they have decided to continue their talks into next week as discussions have been moving along well so far.

Office of Management and Budget Director Frank Raines and Democrats told reporters the day's talks on taxes had not yielded any decisions but had been a full discussion of the issues. Friday's meeting will concern President Clinton's proposals for new spending in education and other areas.
Congressional aides said the decision to hold talks next week was a positive sign.

The top Democrat on the Senate Budget Committee, Sen. Frank Lautenberg told reporters: "I think the positive side of this thing can be clearly seen as one that reflects a degree of cordiality...not just hearing what the other side is saying, but seriously listening."
Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, Republican of New Hampshire, said the tax cut proposals of each side were analyzed for five-year and 10-year costs.
